verdicts.reason: REQ-IF-003 states the byte lane to wdata/rdata mapping; exercised by scenario per lane.
REQ-IF-003 states wstrb[i] enables byte lane i; testable by scenario with varied strobes.
Rule is correct, but the register value is internal state, not an interface signal. It cannot be asserted every cycle from interface signals. It needs write-then-observe scenarios.
REQ-IF-001 states it directly. Output changes can be checked every cycle against clock and reset.
REQ-IF-001 states that no output depends combinationally on any input. MUST_NOT is correct. It is largely the consequence of RF-5-04.
REQ-IF-004 states it directly. It is testable by scenario, varying prot values and checking that outputs are unchanged.

duplicates.reason: Both come from REQ-IF-001. Outputs change only at clock edges or reset, which is the same as no same-cycle combinational dependence on inputs.

questions.question: RF-5-04 says outputs may change when i_rst_n is asserted, which suggests asynchronous reset. Is reset asynchronous or synchronous? That decides whether outputs may change between clock edges on reset assertion.
